notes: Revenue is the club's own release (total revenue £565.3m, the release also calls it 'revenue and other income'); revenue_breakdown 'other' is UEFA prize money (£34.7m) and 'commercial' is commercial revenues and other income. The release gives the loss after tax (£94.7m) but not the pre-tax figure, and no wages; the full annual report PDF on the club site and Companies House is a scanned image, so wages, pre-tax result and attendance are not machine-readable and are left null. ENIC's share count is stated (204,077,955 of 234,811,142 at 5 Sep 2025) but no page states a percentage, so stake_pct is null. Daniel Levy is listed by Forbes as an owner (through ENIC) with no stated stake; he stepped down as Executive Chairman on 4 Sep 2025. Forbes 2026 figures for the same season: revenue $733M (£565M), operating income $139M (£107M), debt/value 38%. Companies House shows further share allotments (7 Oct 2025, 12 Jun 2026); the June 2026 allotment has no club release found. The old record's Deloitte EUR revenue and SI/Yahoo sources were replaced.

ownership_summary: Tottenham Hotspur Limited is majority-owned by ENIC Sports & Development Holdings Ltd, the vehicle of the Lewis family trust, which held 204,077,955 of 234,811,142 ordinary shares at 5 September 2025; the persons with significant control are the trustees' controllers Peter Charrington and Katie Booth. ENIC rejected approaches from PCP and a Firehawk-led consortium in September 2025 and injected £100m of new equity in October 2025; the club and the family say it is not for sale.
